title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
A deployed autonomous vehicle system failed to handle an extreme but foreseeable traffic condition. Multiple Waymo vehicles became unable to move during Fourth of July celebrations in San Francisco when traffic gridlock prevented them from reaching charging stations before their batteries depleted. This is a failure of the system's operational design: it was deployed into an environment where major public events create known, recurring congestion patterns that drain batteries faster than the vehicles can reach safety.

The failure happened in the real world during actual service, not in testing. It would have been caught by stress testing against historical traffic data from major events, battery capacity modeling that accounts for idle time in congestion, and operational limits that prevent deployment during high-risk periods. One vehicle was also damaged when it drove over fireworks on the road, a hazard the system was not designed to navigate.

It is not established whether Waymo's operations planning explicitly considered Fourth of July traffic patterns or whether the company had prior data suggesting this scenario was possible in San Francisco.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations when their batteries drained while stuck in severe traffic. Video footage showed at least a dozen vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up stationary after a fireworks display near the Golden Gate Bridge. The company attributed the incident to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unplanned road closures that created unexpected congestion. Several vehicles required towing assistance. Additionally, one Waymo caught fire after driving over fireworks that someone had set off in the road.

Waymo's roadside assistance team worked to clear the stranded vehicles as the company evaluates ways to improve resilience during major traffic events. Passengers reported frustration and confusion about the situation. San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to meet with stakeholders to improve future traffic management around large public events. This incident follows a December power outage that also affected Waymo's operations in the city when traffic lights went dark.
